name: Bank of Sharjah
founded: 1973 (incorporated by Amiri Decree of the Ruler of Sharjah, 22 Dec 1973; CBUAE banking licence 26 Jan 1974; listed on ADX 2004)
ownership_summary: Listed on ADX; the Government of Sharjah, through Sharjah Asset Management, is the largest shareholder with 39.25% at 31 Dec 2025, after an AED 800m capital increase approved on 4 May 2023 lifted its stake from 17.16% to about 40% and share capital to AED 3bn. United Alsaqer Group (linked to Deputy Chairman Sheikh Saif bin Mohammed bin Butti Al Hamed) holds 9.31%. No ownership change, merger or recapitalisation found for 2024–2026 (checked 2026-10-12).

shareholders.holder: Sharjah Asset Management (Government of Sharjah investment arm)

government_link: Yes — Government of Sharjah via Sharjah Asset Management (39.25% at 31 Dec 2025). The Ruler of Sharjah is Honorary Chairman, the Chairman chairs the Sharjah Finance Department, and the CEO of Sharjah Asset Management sits on the board (board page checked 2026-10-12).
group_structure: Bank of Sharjah P.J.S.C. is the operating bank. Its Lebanese subsidiary, Emirates Lebanon Bank S.A.L. (100%), has been deconsolidated and held for sale since 1 Apr 2023 at AED 844.8m. The sale was still pending at 30 Jun 2026, with several potential buyers under confidentiality agreements, and the auditor added an emphasis of matter. The other subsidiaries are investment, real-estate and Cayman funding vehicles. No wealth, brokerage or asset-management subsidiary was found; private banking and wealth sit inside the bank.

footprint: UAE: six branches in Sharjah, Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain at 30 Jun 2026. PBWM is based in Dubai Media City. Lebanon (Emirates Lebanon Bank) is held for sale.
customer_segments: Mainly wholesale: large and mid-sized corporates, government and semi-government entities (GREs) and financial institutions. A small high-net-worth private banking base (PBWM). A retail banking department was still being set up in 2025–2026, first aimed at owners and employees of the bank's corporate clients, with a premium/wealth focus.
business_lines: Commercial/wholesale banking (largest line), transaction banking (cash management, trade finance), project finance, investment banking (DCM/ECM, M&A finance), treasury, Private Banking & Wealth Management (PBWM, set up 2012; HNW clients; equities, fixed income, mutual funds, structured investments, precious metals), and a retail banking business being built from inception since Aug 2025. Two reported segments: Commercial; Investment and treasury.

capabilities.wealth_summary: Bank of Sharjah calls itself 'predominantly a wholesale bank'. Wealth is a small Private Banking & Wealth Management (PBWM) division, set up in 2012 under a collaboration with Commerzbank International S.A. and based in Dubai Media City. It serves high-net-worth individuals with equities, fixed income, mutual funds, structured investments and precious metals across global and regional markets, plus model portfolios, bespoke strategies and onshore/offshore custody through unnamed partners. The website says the bank is an SCA-licensed portfolio manager that manages portfolios 'based on the choices and instructions of its customers'. The Integrated Report 2025 cites a 2017 strategic partnership with Julius Baer Group, with no detail on its current status. Since Aug 2025, Chief Retail Banking Officer Paul Cox has been building a Retail and Private Banking franchise 'from inception', with a premium offer and an 'increasing emphasis on wealth management and advisory services'. No digital investing channel was found; eBOS is a transactional online and mobile banking app.
